Order Order

 01. 1.

This is an application under Section-439 Cr.P.C.
2.
Heard learned counsel for the parties.
3. The petitioner is an accused in connection with Mangalabag P.S. Case No.19 of 2024 c o r r e s p o n d i n g t o S p e c i a l G . R . C a s e N o .

2 4 o f 2 0 2 4 f o r t h e o f f e n c e s u n d e r Sections-363/366/376(2)(n)/365 of the IPC read with Section 6 of the POCSO Act pending in the Court of the learned A.D.J.-cum-Special Court under POCSO Act, Cuttack.
The petitioner had moved an application before the Court of learned trial Court for grant of bail.
The learned trial Court vide order dated 10.09.2024 rejected his application.
Being aggrieved, the petitioner has filed the present petition under Section 439 Cr.P.C. praying for enlargement on bail.

Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the plea of bail of the petitioner is not pending before any other Court except the present one.
4.

The prosecution case is that the mother of the victim lodged a written report before the concerned Police Station alleging therein that on 18.01.2024 at about 2.00 P.M. she came to know that her minor daughter has been missing from the house.
The informant searched her all around the probable places, but they could not trace her out and her mobile phone was also switched off.
Thereafter, she came to know that the petitioner has taken away her minor daughter to an unknown place.

Hence, the F.I.R.
5.
During investigation, the statement of the victim, who is stated to be 17 years of age, has been recorded under Section 164 of Cr.P.C. and she has also been examined as P.W.1.

In her Ronit Mukhi vs State Of Odisha .... Opp. Party on 4 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/184621920/
1 examination-in-chief, she has stated as under:
"2.

sentences.text: The occurrence took place on 18.01.2024 at about 1.30 A.M. (mid-night).
Out of love I fled away with accused Ronit Mukhi.
First we went to Sambalpur, stayed for one day at Sambalpur then proceed to the house of maternal uncle of accused at Nayagarh.
We stayed for some days at Nayagarh and at that time we were in physical relationship.
Then police bring us back to Mangalabag P.S.
Then I was taken to the Hospital.
I put my signature in a paper at the Hospital.
Ext.P1.P.W.1 is my signature in the consent form along with my endorsement towards my refusal to undergo medical examination.
On the same day later, I again signed on consent from giving my consent for my medical examination.
Ext. P2
/ P.W.1 is my signature.
Then my medical examination was conducted.
Then I was taken to a nearby Ashram and stayed there for one night on the next day at about 3.00 P.M.
I was taken to the Court.
My statement u/s 164 of Cr.P.C. was recorded by the Magistrate.
Ext.P3/P.W.1 and P3/P.W1 are my signatures in the said statement."

From the aforementioned evidence adduced by the prosecution, nature of accusation and age of both the victim ( 17 years) & accused ( 20 years), it can be inferred that this is neither a case of perpetration of sexual exploitation or abuse nor emotional obtrude caused to the vulnerable minor girl, rather it's a case of adolescence love affairs.
The petitioner is aged about 20 years and he is in custody since 01.02.2024.
The victim girl has already been examined Therefore; the accused is entitled to bail.
6. Regard being had to the period of custody of the petitioner from 20.04.2023 and the nature of accusation, age of the petitioner, I am inclined to admit the petitioner to bail.

Hence, the petitioner be released on bail by the learned Court in seisin over the matter in the aforesaid case on such terms and conditions as it would deem just and proper subject to further conditions as following:
(i) The petitioner shall cooperate with the investigation,
(ii) He shall not tamper with the evidence in any manner whatsoever,
(iii) He shall not contact with the victim or her family members, and (iv) He shall not involve in any similar type of offence.
Violation of any conditions of bail shall entail consideration for cancellation of the bail granted to the petitioner.
The prosecution is given liberty to move an application for cancellation of bail before the Court below, if the petitioner violates any conditions of the bail granted to him.
7. The BLAPL is accordingly disposed of.
(S.S. Mishra) Judge amit Location: HIGH COURT OF ORISSA, CUTTACK Ronit Mukhi vs State Of Odisha .... Opp.
